analysis.title: U.S. Equity Factor Insights - October 2026: Stay the Course
key_insights: Barclays keeps all factor views: Positive on Value and Large-over-Small Size, Neutral on Growth, Momentum, Quality and Yield, Negative on High-over-Low Volatility.

Value over Growth: persistent inflation, resilient economic activity and tighter financial conditions are expected to favor Value over the narrow AI-led leadership. Rising funding costs and scrutiny of AI spending raise the odds that performance broadens to cyclical, under-owned segments.
Barclays calls Value an 'anti-AI' style factor. It benefits if leadership broadens beyond AI winners, and it also benefits from its consumer orientation while consumer spending holds up.

Barclays flags widening credit spreads across hyperscaler, data center and neo-cloud issuers, and a material rise in hyperscaler CDS spreads, as credit issuance surges while Treasury yields rise sharply.
Current earnings growth is concentrated in semiconductors, which have had some of the largest forecast errors among S&P 500 industry groups, so it may be vulnerable to downward revisions.

Large-over-Small: higher rates are a headwind for small caps because of their dependence on external financing. The Russell 2000 and S&P 600 are down 7.6% since the end of 1H26 while the S&P 500 is up 4.0%.

Small-cap weakness is broad. Nearly every sector outside Technology has retreated since the 10-year Treasury yield moved above 5%. Barclays rates strategists expect the 10-year to stay near current levels for several quarters.
Small-cap fundamentals are weak: leverage is near post-COVID highs and 33% of Russell 2000 names are unprofitable.

Momentum (Neutral): the factor rose about 10.1% since end of August, driven by semiconductors, electrical equipment and oil & gas, partly offset by software weakness. It is the cheapest style versus its own history. Midterm election years are a threat: in almost every one since 2006 Momentum sold off from early October through November.

Quality (Neutral): FY27 earnings forecasts imply mid-teens growth, and even a significant cut to semiconductor earnings (over 70% of expected earnings growth) would leave double-digit growth. That reduces the need for defensiveness, while election uncertainty keeps demand for quality franchises. Quality has tended to outperform around midterm elections.

High-over-Low Volatility (Negative): the style rebounded in late September but the move faded. It has the lowest share of profitable companies among the styles and has historically struggled in equity drawdowns, so it is exposed to rates, election uncertainty and weak risk appetite.

Yield (Neutral): high risk-free rates limit the appeal of income equities, but Yield is an under-owned 'anti-AI' style with exposure to banks, insurance, oil & gas and software/IT services, and it could gain if AI leadership fades.

September 2026 market performance: S&P 500 -0.5% as banks (-7.3%) and capital markets (-9.9%) offset AI strength. Semiconductors +7.2% and Big Tech +8.1%. Small caps fell 5.4%, led by biotech (-6.0%) and banks (-4.4%).
Russell 1000 Growth gained 2.1% in September versus -3.3% for Russell 1000 Value, driven by semiconductors and TMT exposure.
Over the past month Growth outperformed Value by 5.3%, Momentum rose about 10%, and Large-over-Small gained 3.4% as the 10-year yield moved above 5%.
Barclays forecasts annual AI infrastructure spend rising to over $1.4 trillion by 2028, and Growth is the most crowded style versus its own 10-year history at the 88th percentile.
Q3 2026 sector returns: Energy +16.5%, Utilities -13.0%, Industrials -10.0%, Information Technology +7.0%.

sector_views.rationale: Energy rebounded 16.5% in 3Q26 and has the highest earnings growth and steepest valuation decline among sectors. Momentum and Yield baskets are tilted toward Energy and oil & gas.
The Value basket is tilted toward Financials, which could gain if market leadership broadens. Banks (-7.3%) and capital markets (-9.9%) fell in September.

AI-linked strength drove Growth and Momentum, but Barclays notes semiconductor earnings estimates are vulnerable to downward revisions. Semiconductors account for over 70% of expected earnings growth.
High rates, leverage near post-COVID highs and 33% unprofitable names keep Barclays positive on large caps over small caps.

earnings_insights: Barclays' FY27 earnings forecasts imply mid-teens aggregate S&P 500 growth (Barclays forecast).

Semiconductors account for more than 70% of expected earnings growth. Even a significant downward revision to semiconductor earnings would leave aggregate growth in the double digits (Barclays estimate).
Small-cap earnings growth is expected to pick up over the next few quarters (Barclays chart, 3Q26 to 2Q27 estimates).
Q2 2026 profit margins by sector are shown against Q2 2025. The text says margins for Tech, especially outside Big Tech, far outstrip other sectors.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The yield is above the 5% threshold, which raises financing costs. This is a headwind for small caps and for rate-sensitive sectors, and it supports Large-over-Small and Value.

macro_indicators.reading: Barclays rates strategists expect it to stay around current levels for the next several quarters
macro_indicators.interpretation: Persistently high rates keep the macro backdrop challenging for small caps.

macro_indicators.reading: Markets price between one and two hikes by 2026 year-end. The implied policy rate for mid-2027 has risen by 60 bps in two months.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Supports Value through its consumer orientation.

trade_ideas.description: Long Value / short Growth factor baskets
trade_ideas.rationale: Persistent inflation, resilient growth, rising funding costs and AI spending scrutiny favor Value over the crowded AI-led Growth style.
trade_ideas.risk: Continued AI leadership and strong semiconductor earnings.

trade_ideas.description: Long large caps / short small caps (Large-over-Small Size factor)
trade_ideas.rationale: High rates hurt small caps' financing, and small-cap fundamentals are weak.
trade_ideas.risk: A fall in interest rates would help small caps.

trade_ideas.rationale: The factor struggles in drawdowns and faces headwinds from rates and election uncertainty.

risk_factors: Midterm elections could disrupt prevailing leadership and increase factor volatility.
Rising funding costs and widening credit spreads across hyperscaler, data center and neo-cloud issuers.
Semiconductor earnings revisions: semiconductors have some of the largest forecast errors among S&P 500 industry groups.
Growing scrutiny of AI-related spending and data center politics.
charts_described: Figure 17 plots the 10-year Treasury yield with a current reading of 5.2%.
Figure 14 shows factor crowding percentiles versus 10y history: Growth 88%, Value 83%, Size 67%, Momentum 61%, Volatility 61%, Quality 28%, Yield 23%.
Figure 24 shows the share of unprofitable names in the Russell 2000 at 33%.
Figure 13 shows annual AI infrastructure spend rising from $336B in 2025A to $674B in 2026E, $1,111B in 2027E and $1,430B in 2028E.
vol_and_positioning: Growth is the most crowded style versus its own 10-year history at the 88th percentile. Value is at 83%, Size 67%, Momentum 61%, Volatility 61%, Quality 28% and Yield 23%.
Momentum is the cheapest style versus its own history. It has high exposure to semiconductors, oil & gas and biotech, and is underweight electric utilities, specialty retail and media.
High-over-Low Volatility has the lowest share of profitable companies among the styles and historically struggles in equity drawdowns.
In four of the last five midterm election years, Momentum sold off from September-end through November-end. In the last four midterm years Quality gained over the same period.
Growth and Volatility are highly correlated, as are Value and Yield.
The share of Russell 2000 names with negative earnings is 33%. Small-cap net debt/EBITDA is at its highest since late 2021.
geopolitical: Elevated geopolitical risk in the Middle East supports Momentum's energy exposure.
US midterm elections: Barclays says they could disrupt prevailing market leadership and raise factor volatility.

tension_points.bull_case: Continued earnings strength across AI-linked beneficiaries and Middle East risk support Momentum, and semiconductors drive Growth outperformance. Even with a significant semiconductor revision, aggregate earnings growth stays in double digits.
tension_points.bear_case: Rising funding costs, widening hyperscaler credit spreads, crowded AI positioning and scrutiny of AI spending favor Value and broader leadership. Semiconductor earnings could face downward revisions.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A significant downward revision to semiconductor earnings, or investor fatigue with the AI narrative, would favor Value over Growth. Barclays' Value view would be hurt if AI leadership continues.

tension_points.bull_case: Momentum's AI and energy exposure benefit if current trends persist. Quality has historically outperformed around midterms.
tension_points.bear_case: Momentum sold off from September-end through November-end in four of the last five midterm years, and elections raise factor volatility.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Momentum's neutral stance would change if the midterm-period seasonal pattern fails, or if AI and energy trends clearly persist through the election.
